quests.title: Irodori Poetry: Part III

dialogue.t: Ah, you're here.
Lenne wrote of our regret that we did not meet sooner yesterday, and so today I wish to gift him a verse as well.
Haha, it is my honor to accept such a gift!
Although I'm an old man now, after meeting friends from Mondstadt in recent days, I have grown quite interested in the place.
For this poem, I wrote in imitation of Mondstadt's bards, and the verse will also mention some of that land's scenery.
Unfortunately, I've never been to Mondstadt... But could you help me take a few pictures of <color=#00E1FFFF>Mondstadt's regional specialties</color>?
Haha, in that case, I'll be counting on you. Just like in the previous days, 4 pictures will do the trick.
Well then, how are the pictures coming along?

dialogue.sit: I haven't finished taking them yet.

dialogue.t: I'm sorry for troubling you. What we need today are pictures of <color=#00E1FFFF>Mondstadt's regional specialties</color>. Just as before, <color=#00E1FFFF>4 pictures</color> will do.
Well then, how are the pictures coming along?
Thank you, thank you. Ah, with these, I can finally pen a satisfactory poem down. Now then, let me think...
Here's my draft, written according to the pictures you brought back. Why don't you choose the stanzas we should use?
Indeed, using "tracing the wind's footsteps" as a metaphor for setting off on a journey is a very Mondstadt-like expression.
Connecting a flower to a lover is common to all nations, and this sentence compares remembering the sights of Inazuma to recalling one's first love.

The wild fruit in here must be alluding to some painful experiences. It is not a purely joyful memory, like the first taste of alcohol or the first reading of a poem, but it nonetheless leaves a deep impression.
Ootomo's poem has really broken through the usual form of the Inazuman poem, yet it also uses its ancient style to depict all manner of unforgettable human experiences.

Perhaps he means to say that although Mondstadt and Inazuma may seem greatly different, they do share some common aesthetics — just as how the two of us, despite being from these different nations, were able to bond as poets.
Ah, to think that you were able to grasp the feelings behind this verse so quickly, despite being so young...
I didn't believe in the idea of making friends of disparate ages from yourself before, but now I know that it is true. What a joyful truth it is!
And you too, learned young lady(young man) — that we three should have met here... There must be some destiny at play.
Indeed. The trip to Inazuma was a pretty bumpy one, but none of that matters now. Even when I return to Mondstadt, I will remember everything I've seen here in Inazuma.
This is also thanks to the pictures you brought.
I hope that someday, we three shall meet once again.
We will!
This line says that though one may leave Inazuma, the things one has seen here will remain in one's heart forever.

quests.description: This time, it is Ootomo who wants to try his hand at writing Mondstadt-style poetry. Who knows what literary sparks might fly this time?
